Messages.Author: Mari
Messages.Body:
Hi all,

During a game yesterday, someone had Eternal Vigilance on Lazverinus and
Lazverinus used the EV to untap and block and action. The combat went on and
the acting minion played the Obtenebration Strike:Combat Ends Continue the action card.
Can Lazverinus use the Eternal Vigilance again to untap and block again?

The card text doesn't explicitly state that the EV can only be used once per
action and since it isn't a reaction card, it doesn't fall under the rule of
only being able to use it once per action.

So can a vampire Eternally Vigilate more than once during the same action?

Card Text:

Eternal Vigilance
Card Type: Action
Cost: 1 Blood
Requires a ready Archbishop, Priscus, or Cardinal. +1 stealth.

Put this card on the acting vampire. During an action, the Sabbat vampire with
this card can pay a blood to untap and attempt to block. Burn this card if this
Sabbat vampire goes to torpor.

Thanks!

Mari
Malkavian Admin Assistant for
Portla...@yahoogroups.com
Chatelaine of Portland, OR

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Mari wrote:
> During a game yesterday, someone had Eternal Vigilance on Lazverinus and
> Lazverinus used the EV to untap and block and action. The combat went on and
> the acting minion played the Obtenebration Strike:Combat Ends Continue the action card.
> Can Lazverinus use the Eternal Vigilance again to untap and block again?

No. It uses the "During <X>, do <Y>" template, which limits it to once per action.
Since this is the same action, he cannot untap again with EV.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <9fgvon$cok$1...@taliesin.netcom.net.uk>, Roger Carhult
<rogc...@student.luth.se> writes

>Does that include playing Majesty in a combat and untapping afterwards etc
>as well then? Because doesn't that fit the template you describe too?

One copy of the "During <X>, do Y" text allows you to do <X> once during
any given instance of Y.

If you have more than one card to play, or more than one card to use,
each one of those can count separately.

However, I am at a loss understanding where Majesty comes in. Its card
text is not of the form "During <X>, do <Y>."

I don't see what's confusing about LSJ's answer.

Combat ends resolves before any OTHER strike. That means simultaneous with
other combat end strikes. The side effects of both cards (eg untapping,
getting 1 damage,..) also resolve simultaneously.

Jeroen
